holidays.name: Revenge of the Fifth
holidays.description: Star Wars fans mark May 5 as the Sith's answer to May the Fourth. Expect dark-side movie marathons, villain-themed costumes, and plenty of cheerful menace. The Empire strikes back, but mostly in the form of snacks.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial fan-created observance. It plays on the film title Revenge of the Sith and follows the fan holiday May the Fourth, giving the villains their own day.
holidays.funFact: The film's title, Revenge of the Sith, is what makes May 5 work as the villains' counterpart to May the Fourth.

holidays.name: National Hoagie Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the towering sandwich of cold cuts, cheese, crisp veggies and oil-and-vinegar glory. Whether you call it a hoagie, sub, hero or grinder, today is the day to stack it high and take a big bite.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. The hoagie is closely tied to Philadelphia sandwich culture.
holidays.funFact: The same sandwich goes by many names around the US, including hero, sub, grinder and po'boy, and each region insists its name is the right one.

holidays.name: National Totally Chipotle Day
holidays.description: A smoky salute to the chipotle, the dried, smoked jalapeño that adds deep heat to salsas, marinades, sauces and even chocolate desserts. It shares the calendar with Cinco de Mayo, so it's a good day for spicy snacks.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It sits on May 5 alongside Cinco de Mayo festivities.
holidays.funFact: A chipotle is simply a jalapeño that has been left to ripen, then smoked and dried. The name comes from the Nahuatl word for smoked chili.
